pr_body: Fixes #53715 (see there for the problem description).
pr_comments: I think it should behave the same way. Changed the code to reflect that.

issue_context.title: `#select` generates wrong number of columns when `Arel::Nodes::Quoted` has the same value
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce

```ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true

require "bundler/inline"

gemfile(true) do
  source "https://rubygems.org"

  gem "rails"
  gem "sqlite3"
end

require "active_record"
require "minitest/autorun"
require "logger"

ActiveRecord::Base.establish_connection(adapter: "sqlite3", database: ":memory:")
ActiveRecord::Base.logger = Logger.new(STDOUT)

ActiveRecord::Schema.define do
  create_table :users, force: true
end

class User < ActiveRecord::Base
end

class BugTest < Minitest::Test
  def test_ok
    query = User.all.select([Arel::Nodes::Quoted.new('a'), Arel::Nodes::Quoted.new('b')]).to_sql

    assert_equal("SELECT 'a', 'b' FROM \"users\"", query)
  end

  def test_ng
    query = User.all.select([Arel::Nodes::Quoted.new('a'), Arel::Nodes::Quoted.new('a')]).to_sql

    assert_equal("SELECT 'a', 'a' FROM \"users\"", query)
  end
end
```

### Expected behavior
Pass the tests

### Actual behavior
```
  1) Failure:
BugTest#test_ng:
--- expected
+++ actual
@@ -1 +1 @@
-"SELECT 'a', 'a' FROM \"users\""
+"SELECT 'a' FROM \"users\""
```

### System configuration
**Rails version**: 7.2.1.1

**Ruby version**: 3.2.2
comments: Looks like this is not an easily fixable. Can you describe a real-world example where this is/was a problem?

Here's an example:

```
# frozen_string_literal: true

require "bundler/inline"

gemfile(true) do
  source "https://rubygems.org"

  gem "rails"
  gem "sqlite3"
end

require "active_record"
require "minitest/autorun"
require "logger"

ActiveRecord::Base.establish_connection(adapter: "sqlite3", database: ":memory:")
ActiveRecord::Base.logger = Logger.new(STDOUT)

ActiveRecord::Schema.define do
  create_table :users, force: true do |t|
    t.timestamp :activated_at
    t.timestamp :deleted_at
  end

  create_table :posts, force: true do |t|
    t.string :title
    t.string :body
  end

  create_table :comments, force: true do |t|
    t.string :body
  end

  create_table :notices, force: true do |t|
    t.references :user, foreign_key: true
    t.references :action_user, foreign_key: { to_table: :users }
    t.references :target, polymorphic: true
    t.integer :notice_type, null: false
    t.string :message
  end
end

class User < ActiveRecord::Base
  has_many :notices, dependent: :destroy

  scope :active, -> {
    where.not(activated_at: nil)
     .where(deleted_at: nil)
  }
  scope :notice_recipients, -> (*_args) {
    active
    # Actually, there are some complex search conditions here
  }
end

class Post < ActiveRecord::Base
  def build_notice_message
    "New post!" # Actually, there are some message generation here, i.e. I18n
  end
end

class Comment < ActiveRecord::Base
  def build_notice_message
    "New comment!" # Actually, there are some message generation here, i.e. I18n
  end
end

class Notice < ActiveRecord::Base
  belongs_to :user
  belongs_to :action_user, class_name: 'User'
  belongs_to :target, polymorphic: true

  enum :notice_type, { create_post: 0, create_comment: 1 }

  class << self
    COLUMNS = %i[action_user_id target_type target_id notice_type message].freeze

    def publish_all(notice_type, action_user, target)
      base_attrs = build(action_user:, target:, notice_type:, message: target.build_notice_message).attributes_for_database

      im = Arel::InsertManager.new(arel_table)
      im.ast.columns = [arel_table[:user_id]] + COLUMNS.map { |f| arel_table[f] }
      insert_into = im.to_sql

      recipients = User.notice_recipients(notice_type, action_user, target)
      select_columns = [:id] + COLUMNS.map { |c| Arel::Nodes.build_quoted(base_attrs[c.to_s]) }
      select_from = recipients.select(select_columns).to_sql

      connection.execute("#{insert_into} #{select_from}")
    end
  end
end

class BugTest < Minitest::Test
  def teardown
    Notice.delete_all
    Comment.delete_all
    Post.delete_all
    User.delete_all
  end

  # It usually works fine
  def test_ok
    User.create(id: 1, activated_at: Time.current)
    User.create(id: 2, activated_at: Time.current)
    User.create(id: 3, activated_at: Time.current)
    Post.create(id: 4, title: "Title", body: "Body")
    Notice.publish_all(:create_post, User.find(2), Post.find(4))

    expected = [
      [User.find(1), User.find(2), Post.find(4)],
      [User.find(2), User.find(2), Post.find(4)],
      [User.find(3), User.find(2), Post.find(4)],
    ]
    assert_equal(expected, Notice.all.map { |x| [x.user, x.action_user, x.target] })
  end

  # But, it complains about 'ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid: SQLite3::SQLException: 5 values for 6 columns'
  # in case of some ids are the same value by chance
  # (It also happens when notice_type enum value coincided with other id)
  def test_ng
    User.create(id: 1, activated_at: Time.current)
    User.create(id: 2, activated_at: Time.current)
    User.create(id: 3, activated_at: Time.current)
    Comment.create(id: 2, body: "Comment")
    Notice.publish_all(:create_comment, User.find(2), Comment.find(2))

    expected = [
      [User.find(1), User.find(2), Comment.find(2)],
      [User.find(2), User.find(2), Comment.find(2)],
      [User.find(3), User.find(2), Comment.find(2)],
    ]
    # Fails
    assert_equal(expected, Notice.all.map { |x| [x.user, x.action_user, x.target] })
  end
end
```

----

By the way, I hope to ActiveRecord (or Arel) will support `INSERT INTO ... SELECT FROM ...` syntax somehow.

The specific problem I illustrated was solved by creating a junction table between users and notices.

But still, the original issue seems like a bug to me.
Had you tried https://api.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActiveRecord/Relation.html#method-i-insert_all ? Looks like your are trying to reimplement that method.

Yes, I've already tried it. That looks like:

```Ruby
COLUMNS = %w[action_user_id target_type target_id notice_type message].freeze

def publish_all(notice_type, action_user, target)
  base_attrs = build(action_user:, target:, notice_type:, message: target.build_notice_message)
    .attributes_for_database
    .slice(*COLUMNS)
  User.notice_recipients(notice_type, action_user, target).find_in_batches do |recipients|
    Notice.insert_all(recipients.map { |user| { user_id: user.id, **base_attrs } })
  end
end
```

However, there are some drawbacks to this approach:

- It requires retrieving all recipients from the database.
- It necessitates build large arrays.
- `insert_all` generates very long SQL queries.

As a result, there were performance issues compared to the approach of using `INSERT INTO ... SELECT FORM`.

I opened a PR, I was worrying if it will introduce some unwanted behavior. But all the tests passed and it looks more correct for me to not try be smart by deduplicating selected columns, because it is fine in SQL to provide the same column/expression in `SELECT` multiple times.

review_comments: I'm ok to allow explicit `select(:id, :id)` duplication, but it is not the expected behavior that values that users has not touched are duplicated each time `merge` is called. Fixed by 31d3caece6be5511dbfb5269f926dcf1648b59ac.
